scenes.title: Visual Tokenization: How Multimodal LLMs See Images
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain how vision transformers and patch projection convert raw image pixels into tokens compatible with LLM attention blocks.
scenes.necessity: LLMs operate on discrete sequence tokens. To process images alongside text, visual pixels must be transformed into embedding vectors of the same dimension.
scenes.story: Think of a giant jigsaw puzzle. If you want a language model to read a picture, you can't feed it raw RGB matrix values all at once. You chop the picture into a grid of small square patches, flatten each patch into a vector, and treat every patch as if it were a word token in a sentence.
scenes.narration:
Daksh, Multimodal AI photos ko kaise dekhta hai? Kya use aankhein mil gayi hain?
Nahi dost, use toh sirf tokens samajh aate hain! Isiliye Visual Tokenization hota hai.
Ye kaise hota hai?
Vision Transformer photo ko 16x16 pixels ke chote-chote square tukdo me kaat deta hai. Har tukda ek word vector ban jata hai aur text ke sath hi model ke dimaag me chala jata hai!
scenes.question: How are images tokenized or represented as inputs to a multimodal LLM?
scenes.interview_question: How are images tokenized or represented as inputs to a multimodal LLM?
scenes.interview_view:
Multimodal LLMs (like LLaVA and GPT-4V) use Vision Transformers (ViT) or CLIP vision encoders. The input image is split into non-overlapping patches (e.g., 14x14 pixels), flattened, and linearly projected into visual embedding tokens. A projection layer (linear or MLP) aligns these visual embeddings into the LLM's text embedding space, allowing the LLM decoder to treat image patches as prefix tokens.

scenes.title: Evaluating Image Quality: FID Score and CLIP Score
scenes.teaching_intent: To clarify quantitative metrics for evaluating synthetic image quality and text-image alignment.
scenes.necessity: Unlike text where BLEU or RAGAS evaluate tokens, image generation requires metrics for both visual realism and prompt fidelity.
scenes.story: If an AI generates a photo of a 'cyberpunk cat riding a skateboard', how do you measure if it looks like a real photo versus a blurry mess, and whether the cat is actually on a skateboard?
scenes.narration:
Daksh, AI ki banayi image kitni acchi hai, ye computer kaise naapta hai?
Do metrics hote hain dost: Pehla FID Score (Fréchet Inception Distance) — ye dekhta hai ki image kitni real lag rahi hai. FID jitna kam, image utni zyada asli!
Aur dusra metric?
CLIP Score! CLIP Score dekhta hai ki jo tumne maanga tha (jaise 'Blue Car'), kya photo me wahi bana hai ya kuch aur hi ban gaya!
scenes.question: How do you quantitatively evaluate the quality and prompt alignment of generated images?
scenes.interview_question: How do you quantitatively evaluate the quality and prompt alignment of generated images?
scenes.interview_view:
Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) measures image quality and diversity by comparing feature distributions of generated images against real images extracted from an Inception-v3 pool (lower FID is better). CLIP Score measures text-to-image semantic alignment by computing cosine similarity between the CLIP text embedding of the prompt and the CLIP image embedding of the generated output (higher CLIP score is better).

scenes.title: Serverless GPU vs. Dedicated GPU Instances for LLMs
scenes.teaching_intent: To guide architectural decisions between serverless cold-start inference and dedicated GPU compute instances.
scenes.necessity: GPU instance costs are high. Deciding when to use serverless providers vs. self-hosted GPU clusters impacts unit economics.
scenes.story: Imagine running a taxi service. Option A: buying and parking 5 expensive sports cars in a garage 24/7, paying rent even when no passengers call. Option B: calling a rideshare driver whenever a passenger appears, but waiting 30 seconds for them to arrive.
scenes.narration:
Daksh, Serverless GPU vs Dedicated GPU — apni AI app ke liye kya rent karein?
Agar app nayi hai dost, din me 500 log aate hain aur raat me sab so jaate hain — toh Serverless GPU chuno! Jitne seconds chalega, sirf utna paisa lagega.
Aur agar 24 ghante continuously heavy traffic ho?
Tab Dedicated GPU le lo! Heavy traffic me dedicated sasta padta hai aur cold start ka koi wait nahi karna padta.
scenes.question: Serverless GPU inference vs. always-on dedicated servers — how do you decide?
scenes.interview_question: Serverless GPU inference vs. always-on dedicated servers — how do you decide?
scenes.interview_view:
Serverless GPUs (e.g., Modal, RunPod Serverless, AWS Boto) scale to zero and charge per second of execution, making them ideal for low or unpredictable traffic. However, cold starts (loading multi-gigabyte LLM weights into GPU VRAM) add several seconds of initial latency. Always-on dedicated GPU instances (e.g., AWS g5/p4, RunPod, Lambda Labs) running engines like vLLM or TensorRT-LLM provide minimal latency and lower cost at high, steady request volumes.

scenes.title: Load Balancing & Multi-Provider Failover Architecture
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain resilience patterns for routing LLM traffic across multiple instances and API providers.
scenes.necessity: LLM API outages and rate limits occur frequently. Production architectures require dynamic routing and provider fallback.
scenes.story: Imagine an emergency room dispatch center. If the nearest hospital reaches 100% capacity or loses power, the dispatcher automatically reroutes incoming ambulances to a secondary hospital without stopping traffic.
scenes.narration:
Daksh, Load Balancing aur Multi-Provider Failover kaise kaam karta hai?
Socho ek dukaan par 1000 log aa gaye. Ek hi counter hoga toh bheed lag jayegi. Load Balancer logo ko 3 counters me barabar baant deta hai.
Aur agar ek counter kharab ho jaye?
Toh Load Balancer naye logo ko bache hue 2 counters par bhej deta hai! AI me ye OpenAI, Anthropic aur Groq ke beech traffic divide karta hai.
scenes.question: How do you design load balancing and routing across multiple model replicas or providers?
scenes.interview_question: How do you design load balancing and routing across multiple model replicas or providers?
scenes.interview_view:
Production LLM routers (e.g., LiteLLM, Portkey, custom gateways) sit between client applications and model providers. They enforce token-bucket rate limits, round-robin or least-latency load balancing across GPU replicas, and automatic failover fallback chains (e.g., primary OpenAI -> secondary Anthropic -> local vLLM). Circuit breakers prevent cascading failures by temporarily routing away from degraded endpoints.

What would you optimize first if cost doubled without a quality change?

scenes.title: Implementing Exponential Backoff with Jitter for LLM APIs
scenes.teaching_intent: To teach resilient API retry patterns with randomized jitter to prevent thundering herd problems during rate limits.
scenes.necessity: Transient 429 and 503 errors are common when calling LLM APIs. Naive retry loops crash servers with synchronized retries.
scenes.story: If a door is temporarily locked and 100 people all try to turn the handle every exact 2 seconds, the door stays jammed. If everyone waits a random amount of time between 1 and 5 seconds, people slip through smoothly one by one.
scenes.narration:
Daksh, Exponential Backoff with Jitter kya hota hai? Jab API error 429 aaye tab kya kare?
Jab server kahe 'Bohot bheed hai, thodi der ruko', toh har millisecond par dobara darwaza mat khatkhatao, nahi toh ban ho jaoge!
Toh kitna wait kare?
Exponential Backoff kehta hai — pehle 1 second ruko, fir 2 second, fir 4 second, fir 8 second! Aur Jitter matlab thoda sa random time jod do (jaise 2.3 seconds) taaki saare users ek hi pal me dobara hamla na bol dein!
scenes.question: How do you implement an exponential backoff retry wrapper with jitter for flaky LLM API calls?
scenes.interview_question: How do you implement an exponential backoff retry wrapper with jitter for flaky LLM API calls?
scenes.interview_view:
Exponential backoff increases wait time exponentially between retries (e.g., 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s). Full jitter adds a random delay between 0 and the exponential cap: sleep = random_uniform(0, min(max_delay, base_delay * 2^attempt)). This spreads out retries across client instances, preventing thundering herd spikes on rate-limited endpoints. Non-retryable errors (e.g., 400 Bad Request or 401 Unauthorized) should fail fast without retrying.

scenes.title: Token-Bucket Rate Limiter for LLM Applications
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain the mechanics of a token-bucket rate limiter algorithm for controlling outbound API request bursts and throughput.
scenes.necessity: LLM providers enforce Strict Requests-Per-Minute (RPM) and Tokens-Per-Minute (TPM). Rate limiters protect infrastructure from ban blocks.
scenes.story: Imagine an arcade machine that holds up to 10 tokens. Every second, 1 token drops into the coin slot automatically. You can spend 5 tokens at once in a quick burst, but once empty, you must wait for tokens to refill.
scenes.narration:
Daksh, Token-Bucket Rate Limiter kaise kaam karta hai?
Socho ek baalti hai dost, jisme har second 10 paani ki boondein (tokens) girti hain. Baalti me max 100 boondein aa sakti hain.
Aur jab user request bhejta hai?
Toh wo 1 boond nikaal leta hai. Agar baalti me paani hai toh request pass ho jayegi. Agar user ne ek second me 200 requests bhej di, toh baalti khali ho jayegi aur use 'Rate Limit' ka board dikh jayega!
scenes.question: How do you implement a token-bucket rate limiter for outgoing LLM API calls?
scenes.interview_question: How do you implement a token-bucket rate limiter for outgoing LLM API calls?
scenes.interview_view:
A token-bucket rate limiter tracks current token capacity up to a maximum bucket size. Tokens refill continuously over time: tokens = min(capacity, current_tokens + (now - last_refill) * refill_rate). When a request arrives, if tokens >= required_cost, tokens are decremented and the request proceeds; otherwise, the request is delayed or rejected. This allows short bursts up to capacity while strictly enforcing long-run average throughput.

scenes.title: Triage Scenario: Non-Deterministic Output Drift
scenes.teaching_intent: To provide a structured diagnostic methodology for debugging output drift in production LLM applications.
scenes.necessity: Users reporting different answers to identical prompts minutes apart indicates unconstrained sampling or dynamic prompt injection.
scenes.story: A user asks a support bot 'What is the refund policy?' at 10:00 AM and gets a clear 3-bullet summary. They ask the exact same question at 10:05 AM and get a vague 4-paragraph essay. What went wrong?
scenes.narration:
Daksh, achanak hamare AI ke answers me drift aa gaya aur wo ajeeb baatein kar raha hai! Isse kaise theek kare?
Sabse pehle 3 cheezein check karo dost! Pehla — kya kisi ne system prompt me koi naya word daal diya?
Dusra kya check kare?
Kya provider ne model version silently update kar diya? Hamesha 'gpt-4o-2024-08-06' jaisa pinned version use karo. Aur teesra — RAG logs dekho ki kya koi nayi gandi file database me chali gayi hai!
scenes.question: Users report that the chatbot gives noticeably different answers to the exact same question asked minutes apart. How do you debug this?
scenes.interview_question: Users report that the chatbot gives noticeably different answers to the exact same question asked minutes apart. How do you debug this?
scenes.interview_view:

(2) Dynamic Context / RAG — verify if retrieved context chunks or timestamps changed between calls. (3) System Prompt / History — check if un-truncated chat history or dynamic system prompts are shifting. (4) Seed / Model Routing — check if multi-provider load balancers routed to different model snapshots (e.g., gpt-4o vs gpt-4o-mini).

Interview perspective:
A strong interview answer should define what is being measured, how the evaluation set is built, how regressions are detected, and how traces connect an incorrect answer to retrieval, model, tool, or application behavior. Mention human review where automated metrics are insufficient.

How would you distinguish model regression from retrieval or data regression?
What traces and metrics would you capture in production?

Agar input tokens se bada ho toh?

scenes.title: System Design: Grounded Help-Center Chatbot
scenes.teaching_intent: To walk through an end-to-end production architecture for a grounded documentation assistant.
scenes.necessity: Building a production RAG chatbot requires integrating ingestion, vector search, re-ranking, guardrails, and analytics.
scenes.story: An enterprise wants an instant AI assistant for 50,000 help center articles. It must answer accurately, cite exact articles, and never leak internal confidential draft documents.
scenes.narration:
Daksh, ek company ke liye 100% reliable Help-Center Chatbot kaise banayein?
Aasan architecture dost: Aage Rate Limiter aur Guardrails. Beech me Hybrid RAG jo company FAQs se sach nikaale.
Aur agar bot ko answer na pata ho?
Toh wo jhooth na bole! Ek confidence score set karo. Agar score kam ho, toh chat turant ek real human agent ko transfer ho jaye. Customer bhi khush, company bhi safe!
scenes.question: How do you design an end-to-end grounded customer-support chatbot for company documentation?
scenes.interview_question: How do you design an end-to-end grounded customer-support chatbot for company documentation?
scenes.interview_view:
A production help-center chatbot architecture consists of: (1) Ingestion Pipeline — header-based semantic chunking, vector embedding, and automated sync jobs. (2) Retrieval Layer — hybrid search (BM25 + HNSW) followed by cross-encoder re-ranking. (3) Guardrails & Generation — input prompt injection checks, system prompt with 'answer only from context' constraint, and output groundedness evaluation. scenes.teaching_intent: To teach candidates how to structure project walkthroughs highlighting trade-offs, engineering decisions, and quantitative evaluation.
scenes.necessity: Interviewers evaluate senior candidates on concrete architectural decisions, failures, and metrics rather than high-level tutorial summaries.
scenes.story: When asked 'Walk me through a RAG system you built,' saying 'I used LangChain and OpenAI' sounds like a beginner tutorial. Saying 'We processed 100k PDFs, used hybrid search with BGE-reranker, and improved faithfulness from 72% to 94%' proves production expertise.

scenes.question: How do you walk through a RAG system you built end-to-end in an interview?
scenes.interview_question: How do you walk through a RAG system you built end-to-end in an interview?

(3) Key Failure & Iteration — share a real production issue (e.g., table parsing failure, low precision) and how you solved it. (4) Quantitative Impact — state concrete metrics (e.g., latency reduction, cost savings, RAGAS faithfulness score improvement).

scenes.title: Handling AI System Outage and Toxic Outputs
scenes.teaching_intent: To evaluate incident response, root-cause analysis, and mitigation when an AI application produces wrong or harmful outputs.
scenes.necessity: GenAI applications occasionally produce bad outputs. Showing structured incident resolution demonstrates engineering maturity.
scenes.story: A financial advisor AI bot tells a client to invest their life savings in a meme coin due to a hallucination. The client posts a screenshot on Twitter. What do you do in the first 60 minutes?
scenes.narration:
Daksh, agar AI system aadhi raat ko toxic ya galat jawab dene lage, toh kya kare?
Emergency protocol follow karo dost! Step 1 — Containment! Turant gateway se model ka switch off karke safe static message par fallback kar do.
Step 2 kya hai?
Root Cause Analysis! Raat ke Traces kholo — kya prompt injection hua ya galat document upload hua? Aur Step 3 — Us attack ko test suite me add karke fix karo aur tabhi system dobara live karo!
scenes.question: Tell me about a time an AI system you built produced a wrong or harmful output. What did you do?
scenes.interview_question: Tell me about a time an AI system you built produced a wrong or harmful output. What did you do?
scenes.interview_view:
Answer using the STAR-Incident framework: (1) Containment — immediately trigger guardrail blocks or fallback routing to mitigate ongoing risk. (2) Root Cause Analysis — trace the request telemetry log (input prompt, retrieved chunks, temperature, model version). (3) Structural Fix — ship regression test cases to the offline eval suite, update guardrail classifiers or prompt constraints. (4) Post-Mortem — document lessons learned and establish automated monitoring alerts to prevent recurrence.

Interview perspective:
Interviewers usually care about the application boundary, not only the model. Separate untrusted input from system instructions, validate tool arguments server-side, enforce least privilege, protect sensitive data, log safely, and define explicit refusal/fallback paths.

What failure mode would you watch for?

scenes.title: Resolving Technical Disagreements in GenAI Teams
scenes.teaching_intent: To demonstrate constructive technical collaboration, data-driven decision making, and alignment on team goals.
scenes.necessity: Engineers often disagree on architectures (e.g., Fine-tuning vs. RAG). Resolving disputes via empirical data shows leadership.
scenes.story: One senior engineer wants to spend 3 months fine-tuning a custom LLaMA model. Another wants to launch a simple RAG pipeline in 2 weeks. How do you resolve the deadlock?
scenes.narration:
Daksh, jab AI team me do engineers lad padein — ek kahe 'fine-tuning karo', dusra kahe 'RAG karo' — toh faisla kaise karein?
Behas me kabhi ego mat lao dost! Data-driven decision making karo. Dono se kaho — '100 sawalo ka ek test benchmark banao!'
Aur dono methods ko test karein?
Haan! Ek engineer 3 din me RAG ka prototype banaye, dusra LoRA model banaye. Fir Accuracy, Cost, Latency aur maintenance naapo. Jo data me jeetega, wahi production me jayega!
scenes.question: Tell me about a technical conflict you had with a teammate or manager and how you resolved it.
scenes.interview_question: Tell me about a technical conflict you had with a teammate or manager and how you resolved it.
scenes.interview_view:

(2) Run a rapid prototype / benchmark — test both approaches on a representative dataset rather than arguing hypothetically. (3) Align on business outcomes — pick the option that satisfies immediate user needs while keeping architectural flexibility for future iterations.

scenes.title: The GenAI Master Glossary: Core Formulas & Terms
scenes.teaching_intent: To summarize foundational terms, formulas, and concepts for rapid interview review.
scenes.necessity: Quick-reference term mastery enables clear, concise communication during technical interview rounds.
scenes.story: Before walking into the interview room, you do a 2-minute mental scan of the core equations, model types, and key algorithms that form the bedrock of AI engineering.
scenes.narration:
Congratulations dost! Hum 78th scene par pahuch gaye! Chalo ek quick game khelte hain — AI ke 3 sabse bade formulas!
Chalo Daksh, pehla formula batao!
Attention Formula — Softmax of (Q times K-transpose divided by square root of d-k) times V! Ye hai Transformer ka dil!
Dusra formula?
LoRA Update — W = W0 + (B * A) * (alpha / r)! Jahan bade model ko chhedhe bina choti matrix se training hoti hai.
Aur teesra formula?
Cosine Similarity — A dot B divided by (norm A times norm B)! Jisse do words ke beech ka meaning aur distance naapa jata hai. Poora AI Engineering inhi par tika hai!
scenes.question: What are the essential rapid-fire terms and formulas every GenAI engineer must know?
scenes.interview_question: What are the essential rapid-fire terms and formulas every GenAI engineer must know?
scenes.interview_view:
Core terms: (1) Scaled Dot-Product Attention: softmax(Query times Key-transpose / square root of d-k) V. (2) Decoder-Only: Causal attention, autoregressive text generation (GPT-4, LLaMA 3, Claude 3.5). (3) Encoder-Only: Bidirectional attention, representation learning (BERT). (4) KV Cache: Stores Key/Value tensors in GPU VRAM to avoid O(n^2) redundant computation during generation. (5) LoRA: Freezes pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank rank-decomposition matrices (A and B). (6) DPO: Direct Preference Optimization without a separate reward model.

scenes.title: Context Engineering: Building the Right Context, Not Just the Right Prompt
scenes.teaching_intent: To distinguish prompt wording from the broader engineering problem of selecting, ordering, compressing, retrieving, validating, and updating the context supplied to an LLM.
scenes.necessity: Production LLM quality often depends on what information reaches the model, not just how the instruction is phrased.
scenes.story: A model can have a great prompt and still fail if the context contains stale documents, irrelevant chunks, noisy tool output, or too much history.
scenes.narration: Prompt likhna sirf ek part hai. Production system me asli question hai: model ko exactly kaunsi information, kis order me, kitni quantity me aur kis source se deni hai? Isi broader problem ko context engineering ke lens se dekha ja sakta hai.
scenes.question: What is context engineering, and how is it different from prompt engineering?
scenes.interview_question: What is context engineering, and how is it different from prompt engineering?
scenes.interview_view:
Context engineering treats the model's full input as an engineered state: system instructions, user input, retrieved evidence, tool results, memory, constraints, and conversation history. The goal is to supply the right information in the right structure and order while controlling noise, token usage, freshness, and safety.

scenes.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): Standardizing Model-to-Tool Connections
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain MCP as a standardized way for AI applications to discover and interact with external tools and data sources.
scenes.necessity: As agents connect to many tools, bespoke integrations become difficult to maintain, secure, and reuse.
scenes.story: Imagine every AI application inventing its own format for connecting to databases, files, APIs, and developer tools. MCP addresses this integration problem with a common protocol pattern.
scenes.narration: Function calling model ko bolta hai ki 'mujhe ye tool call karna hai'. MCP broader connection layer ko standardize karta hai — AI application aur external tools/data ke beech integration ko consistent banane ke liye.
scenes.question: What is MCP, and how is it different from ordinary function calling?
scenes.interview_question: What is MCP, and how is it different from ordinary function calling?
scenes.interview_view:
MCP is an open protocol for connecting AI applications with external tools and data through standardized client-server interactions. Function calling describes how a model can request a tool; MCP standardizes more of the surrounding connection and discovery pattern. Production systems still need authentication, authorization, input/output validation, auditing, rate limits, and least-privilege access.

Interview perspective:
For a production answer, describe the control loop and boundaries: model decision, tool schema, authorization, execution, result validation, iteration limits, timeout/error handling, and observability. Also explain when a deterministic workflow is preferable to an agent.
interview_followups: When would you use a deterministic workflow instead of an agent?
How would you limit tool permissions and prevent unsafe actions?
How would you handle tool failure, loops, timeouts, and unexpected tool output?
scenes.production_angle: Permissions, validation, bounded execution, observability, failure recovery, and cost.

scenes.title: Reliable LLM API Contracts: Structured Output Is Not Business Validation
scenes.teaching_intent: To teach the difference between schema-constrained output and actual application correctness.
scenes.necessity: A valid JSON object can still contain incorrect, unsafe, incomplete, or unauthorized values.
scenes.story: Suppose an LLM returns perfectly valid JSON with an account ID and refund amount. The JSON parser succeeds, but should your system immediately issue the refund? Definitely not.
scenes.narration: JSON valid aa gaya matlab answer correct hai — ye assumption dangerous hai. Schema shape validate karta hai; business correctness aur authorization application ko enforce karna chahiye.
scenes.question: If an LLM returns schema-valid structured output, what still needs to be validated?
scenes.interview_question: If an LLM returns schema-valid structured output, what still needs to be validated?

Structured output can enforce a response shape, but application code must still validate required fields, ranges, authorization, business rules, state transitions, external identifiers, and tool permissions. scenes.title: Agent vs. Workflow: When Not to Use an Agent
scenes.teaching_intent: To teach the architectural boundary between deterministic workflows and adaptive agents.
scenes.necessity: Using an agent where the steps are already known can add unnecessary latency, cost, nondeterminism, and security complexity.
scenes.story: If a task is always 'validate input → retrieve record → call API → format response', making an LLM decide every next step may create more problems than it solves.
scenes.narration: Agar steps already fixed hain, agent lagana intelligence nahi — unnecessary complexity ho sakta hai. Agent tab useful hai jab next action actually dynamic ho.
scenes.question: When should you use a deterministic workflow instead of an agent?
scenes.interview_question: When should you use a deterministic workflow instead of an agent?
scenes.interview_view:
Use a workflow when the sequence and branching logic are sufficiently known and can be represented explicitly. Use an agent when the next action depends materially on observations, tool results, or dynamic planning. Agents introduce additional model calls, failure modes, permissions, and nondeterminism, so they should earn their complexity.

Interview perspective:

scenes.title: Production Debugging: The LLM System Is Wrong—Where Do You Start?
scenes.teaching_intent: To teach a systematic debugging approach for nondeterministic or multi-component LLM applications.
scenes.necessity: An incorrect answer can originate in input, retrieval, reranking, context construction, model generation, tools, post-processing, or business logic.
scenes.story: A user reports that the chatbot suddenly started giving wrong answers. Restarting the model is not a debugging strategy. First preserve the exact request and trace the complete execution path.
scenes.narration: LLM wrong answer ko directly model bug mat bolo. Pehle exact request, context, retrieval, tool calls aur model version capture karo; phir pipeline ko stage by stage isolate karo.
scenes.question: An LLM application suddenly produces wrong answers in production. How would you debug it?
scenes.interview_question: An LLM application suddenly produces wrong answers in production. How would you debug it?
scenes.interview_view:
First reproduce the request and preserve the relevant model/version, prompt, parameters, context, retrieved documents, reranker output, tool calls, tool results, and post-processing. Then isolate each stage: input/context, retrieval, generation, tools, and application logic. Compare against a known-good evaluation set and recent traces to identify regression, data drift, provider changes, or application bugs. Sensitive data in traces must be protected.

Interview perspective:
A strong interview answer should define what is being measured, how the evaluation set is built, how regressions are detected, and how traces connect an incorrect answer to retrieval, model, tool, or application behavior. Mention human review where automated metrics are insufficient.
interview_followups: What would you put in an evaluation set before changing the system?
How would you distinguish model regression from retrieval or data regression?
What traces and metrics would you capture in production?
